observations.meaning: Resolve FileScope.temp through FilePathManager.getLocalPath, resolve multipart, create directories with Files.createDirectories, and set MultipartConfigFactory location to Path.toString.
Read spring.servlet.multipart.file-size-threshold from Environment, fall back only on null to 2MB, parse DataSize, and call setFileSizeThreshold.
Read spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size from Environment, fall back only on null to 100MB, parse DataSize, and call setMaxFileSize.
Read spring.servlet.multipart.max-request-size from Environment, fall back only on null to 100MB, parse DataSize, and call setMaxRequestSize.

environment_lookup.nullable_fallback: Only a null lookup uses the supplied fallback. Blank or malformed non-null values reach DataSize.parse and fail. Do not silently turn them into default or unlimited configuration.

original_location.creation_failure: Propagate directory creation failure; do not silently use a different location.

supplier_effective_observation.basis: Exact SizeLimitExceededException permitted maximum in the diagnostic HTTP response. This does not claim a separately exercised max-file-size boundary.

configuration_values.configuration_loading: Spring Boot 2.3.4 explicit spring.config.location replaces default search locations. An application not loading stock classpath application.yml can use native fallback values unless another environment source overrides them. Runtime effective values must not be inferred solely from a bundled file.

prior_owned_difference.effect: Use servlet-default temporary location, immediate disk threshold and unlimited file/request sizes; ignore original Environment configuration.

diagnostic_http_before.body_framing: The control sends a complete 117-byte multipart body with matching Content-Length. The upper-limit diagnostic deliberately declares 1073741825 bytes while sending only the same 117-byte multipart body; it uses an ordinary HTTPConnection without write-half-close.
diagnostic_http_before.parsing_entry: In the supplier observed stack, DefaultTokenBasedRememberMeServices.autoLogin calls getParameter before MVC dispatch; Tomcat multipart parsing enforces the configured length limit there.
diagnostic_http_before.interpretation: The matching small controls and exact configured maximum in the supplier exception demonstrate a container multipart configuration difference. Owned parses the tiny terminal boundary and returns data while its request limit is unlimited.
limits: This is not a valid complete 1GiB upload, nor a file-size boundary test.
HTTP500 is original supplier exception behavior, not a status chosen as an improvement.
Diagnostic responses and static attribution do not establish strict API closure.

container_ordering.source_of_identity: Selected Spring 5.2.9, Boot 2.3.4 and Tomcat 9.0.64 public JAR hashes exactly match stock BOOT-INF/lib members.
container_ordering.eager_mvc_path: DispatcherServlet.checkMultipart precedes handler lookup and MVC interceptors when reached; security filters can call getParameter/getParts earlier.
container_ordering.known_length_rejection: Tomcat FileItemIteratorImpl.init compares known Content-Length with sizeMax and throws SizeLimitExceededException before its first getInputStream call.
container_ordering.temporary_parts: Normal parsing may spool parts to temporary disk. Spring cleanupMultipart deletes file Parts after dispatch; FileUploadBase also attempts deletion of accumulated items after parse failure. Actual cleanup requires observation.

replacement.behavior: Restore the original directory and three Environment-backed DataSize settings using public Java and Spring APIs. Preserve controlled configuration overrides and failure semantics; do not restore native initialization, license checks, MAC checks or native termination paths.

analysis_method: Exact stock Java method declaration inspection without class execution
Complete exact-symbol native disassembly without native execution
Original FilePathManager/SystemUtils chain and public Spring/Tomcat bytecode
Four existing real HTTP observations before repair
limitations: No new API pass is generated by this provenance.
No stock private class or native input enters the distribution.
A normal small multipart read and cleanup check remain necessary runtime validation; the intentionally short-body diagnostic alone does not establish cleanup or full payload handling.
